artworks.title: Aethra Showing her Son Theseus the Place Where his Father had Hidden his Arms
artworks.description: Brenet's Troezen — Aethra shows Theseus where Aegeus hid the sword and sandals, the tokens that start the Isthmus road.

artworks.title: Theseus Finding his Father's Sword (Thésée retrouve l'épée de son père)
artworks.description: Poussin and Lemaire — Theseus recovering his father's arms under the rock, then turning toward Athens on foot.

artworks.title: Theseus and Pirithous Clearing the Earth of Brigands
artworks.description: Mongez's brigand-clearing — Theseus and Pirithous making the road safe, the labours that name the journey to Athens.

artworks.title: Theseus Recognized by his Father
artworks.description: Flandrin's recognition — Theseus known by Aegeus at Athens, the road's end when the sword proves the son.

popCulture.title: Theseus
popCulture.description: The rock at Troezen, then the Isthmus road — Periphetes, Sinis, Cercyon, Procrustes: the labours that made Athens' hero.

popCulture.title: Procrustes
popCulture.description: The iron bed on the road to Athens — still the name for forcing everything to one measure.
